headword: Ìjàpá ní òun tí ìbá só ló sùn yìí, bẹ́ẹ̀ni ẹní bá sùn kì í só.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Tortoise argues that it that might have farted is sound asleep, and, surely, those that sleep do not fart!", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ìjàpá ń lọ sájò, wọ́n ní ìgbà wo ni yó dèé, ó ní ó dìgbàtí òun bá tẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Tortoise set out on a journey and it was asked when it would return; it replied that it would be after it had earned disgrace.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àjátì àwọ̀n ní ń kọ́ òrofó lọ́gbọ́n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a loosely hung net that teaches the fruit pigeon a lesson.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ń pa ẹmọ́n; à-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ń pa àfè; à-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ń pa máláàjú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Feeding-without-leaving kills the Tullberg's rat; feeding-without-departing kills the spotted grass mouse; feeding-without-departing kills the máláàjú rat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-jẹ-pọ̀ ni tàdán.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Eating-until-vomiting is the trait of the bat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-jẹ-tán, à-jẹ-ì-mọra, ká fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá jẹun ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Eating-absolutely-everything, eating-with-abandon, eating with all ten fingers is unworthy of human beings.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-jókòó-àì-dìde, à-sọ̀rọ̀-àì-gbèsì, ká sinni títí ká má padà sílé, àì-sunwọ̀n ní ń gbẹ̀yìn-in rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Sitting-without-getting-up, speaking-without-waiting-for-responses, walking people on their way and not turning back, unpleasantness is what they breed.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ń gbé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The hedgehog does not live in the grassland, only in the forest.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àkàtàm̀pò ò tó ìjàá jà; ta ní tó mú igi wá kò ó lójú?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The bow cannot fight, but who dares confront it with a stick?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àkíìjẹ́ mú òrìṣà níyì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Refusal-to-acknowledge-salutations enhances the god's dignity.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àkísàá mọ ìwọ̀n araa rẹ̀, ó gbé párá jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The rag knows its place; it remains quietly on the rafters.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àkókó inú igbó ní àwọ́n lè gbẹ́ odó; ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ lódòó ní àwọ́n lè lọ́ ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; awúrebé ní àwọ́n lè hun aṣọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Woodpeckers in the forest say they can carve mortars, frogs in the stream say they can string beads, and awúrebe say they can weave cloth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Akórira ò ní nǹkan; ọ̀dùn ò sunwọ̀ fún ṣòkòtò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An overly squeamish person owns nothing; raffia cloth is no good for trousers.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Akú, n kò ní omitooroo rẹ̀ ẹ́ lá; àìkú, n kò níí pè é rán níṣẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Dead, I will not eat its broth; alive, I will not send it on an errand.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àkùkọ̀ adìyẹ́ fi dídájí ṣàgbà; ó fi ṣíṣu-sílẹ̀ ṣèwe.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The rooster shows its maturity by its early rising; it shows its lack of maturity by defecating on the floor.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláìnítìjú lọ kú sílé ànaa rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A shameless person goes to die in his relative-in-laws' house.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláǹgbá kì í lérí àti pa ejò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A lizard does not boast that it will kill a snake.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláàńtètè: ó jí ní kùtùkùtù ó ní òun ó dàá yànpọ̀n-yànpọ̀n sílẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cricket arises in the morning and vows to perform wonders.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣejù ajá ní ń lépa ẹkùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is an overreaching dog that chases leopards.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣejù ní ń gbẹ́bọ kọjá ìdí èṣù; a-gbé-sàráà-kọjá-a-mọ́ṣáláṣí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is an immoderate person who carries his offering past Èṣù's shrine; one-who-carries-his-alms-past-the-mosque.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣejù, pẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ńtẹ́; àṣéjù, baba àṣetẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The immoderate person easily finds disgrace; immoderation is the father of disgrace.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣejù tí ń pọkọ ní baba.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Overzealous wife that calls her husband “father.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣọ àlà kì í jókòó sísọ̀ elépo.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person dressed in white does not sit at the stall of a palm-oil seller.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣọ kan kì í ná ànárẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who has only one set of clothing does not bargain until he is wet.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aláṣọ kan kì í ṣeré òjò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who has only one set of clothing does not play in the rain.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Alátiṣe ní ń mọ àtiṣe araa rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person who must settle his/her affair knows best how he/she plans to go about doing so.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àmọ̀tẹ́kùn fara jọ ẹkùn, kò lè ṣe bí ẹkùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The àmọ̀tẹ́kùn looks like a leopard, but it cannot do what a leopard can do.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Amùrín ò sunwọ̀n, ó yí sáró.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The lizard is not good-looking to start with, and it slips into indigo dye.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ànámánàá ẹtù jìnfìn; ònímónìí ẹtù jìnfìn; ẹran mìíràn ò sí nígbó lẹ́yìn ẹtù?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Yesterday the antelope was caught in a pit-trap; today the antelope is caught in a pit-trap; is there no other animal in the forest besides the antelope?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àpárá ńlá, ìjà ní ń dà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Excessive ribbing unfailingly leads to a fight.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àpárá ńlá ni iná ń dá; iná ò lè rí omi gbéṣe.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The fire is being most overbearing; there is nothing fire can do to water.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àpárá ńlá nikán ń dá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The termite is being most overbearing; a termite cannot eat a rock.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àpọ́nlé ni “İyáa Káà”; ìyá kan ò sí ní káà tí kò lórúkọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Calling a person “Mother of the Compound” is only a mark of respect; there is no mother in the compound who does not have a name.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àpọ́nlé ni “Fọ́maàn”; ẹnìkan ò lè ṣe èèyàn mẹ́rin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Calling a person a foreman is only a mark of respect; nobody can be four men.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ara okó ní òun gbọ́ fínrín fínrín; ta ló sọ fun bí kò ṣe ará ile?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The bush dweller says he heard a rumour; who told him, if it was not a town dweller?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ara-àìbalẹ̀, olórí àrùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Restlessness, father of all diseases.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé ṣu sápẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house shits in the sauce-pan.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àrí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé yọkun lémú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house walks around with mucus dripping from his nose.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àrífín ilé ò jẹ́ ká jẹ òròmọ adìyẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Fear of losing face within one's home dissuades one from eating day-old chicks.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Arọ̀lẹ̀kẹ̀ ò rọ bàtà; gbẹ́dó-gbẹ́dó ò rọ ojúgun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The bead maker cannot fashion a shoe; the mortar carver cannot manufacture a shinbone.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: A-ṣe-bọ̀rọ̀kìnní-má-kìíyè-sábíyá, gbogbo abíyá dọ́ṣẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "He-who-lives-in-style-but-pays-no-attention-to-his-armpits, both armpits are taken over with foamy filth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àṣejù baba àṣetẹ́; ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ń gbẹ̀yìn àṣejù; àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Lack of moderation is the father of disgrace; disgrace comes of immoderation; a grown person who clothes himself in immoderation will find disgrace.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-sẹ́-kú làgbàlagbà ń sẹ́ ọ̀ràn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Denying-until-death is the way a venerable person denies a matter.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀yọ màrìwò, ó ní òun ó kan ọ̀run; àwọn aṣáájúu rẹ̀ ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ rí?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The newly emerged palm frond says it will touch the sky; did those that came before it do so?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀yọ ọ̀gọmọ̀ ó ní òun ó kan ọ̀run; àwọn aṣáájúu rẹ̀ ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ rí?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "This is a variant of the previous entry, using a different name, ọ̀gọmọ̀, for palm frond.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aṣọ à-fọ̀-fún ò jẹ́ ká mọ olówó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Clothes washed clean make identifying the rich person impossible.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aṣọ tó kuni kù ní ń jẹ́ gọgọwú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever clothing one is left with is one's best.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: A-ṣúra-mú ò tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who is mindful of his/her image is not easily disgraced.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-tẹ́-ẹ̀-ká ni iyì ọlọ́lá; sálúbàtà ni iyì ọlọ̀tọ̀; bá a bá gbéra lágbèéjù ọba ni wọ́n ń finí i ṣe
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Spreading-the-mat-without-rolling-it-back-up is the mark of the wealthy; sandals are the mark of the illustrious; if one sings one's praise too loudly one is liable to be made a king.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: À-wín-ná-wó ò yẹni; à-gbà-bọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn; bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a dòrògí; ohun ẹni ní ńyẹni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Borrowing-money-to-spend does not speak well of one; borrowed trousers do not become a person; if it is not tight around the legs it is difficult to remove; it is one's thing that fits one.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: A-wọ̀lú-má-tẹ̀ẹ́, ìwọ̀n araa rẹ̀ ló mọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One-who-enters-a-town-and-maintains-his/her-reputation does because he/she knows his/her place.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àwúrèbeé ní òún lè yẹ̀nà; ta ní jẹ́ tọ ọ̀nà àwúrèbe?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Àwúrebe says it can make a path; who would wish to follow a path it makes?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àáyá yó níjọ́ kan, ó ní ká ká òun léhín ọ̀kánkán.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The Colobus monkey ate its fill one day, and asked that his front teeth be knocked out.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aáyán ati eèrà ṣígun, wọ́n ní àwọ́n ń lọ mú adìẹ àlọ la rí, a ò rábọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Cockroach and ant make ready for war and say they are off to capture chicken; we see their departure, but not their return.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aáyán fẹ́ jó; adìẹ ni ò jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cockroach would dance; it is the chicken that does not allow.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Aáyán kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ erin; èèyàn kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ irò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A cockroach does not trip an elephant; a human being does not trip a chimpanzee.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ayọ̀ àyọ̀jù làkèré fi ń ṣẹ́ nítan.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is excessive rejoicing that breaks the frog's thigh.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Àyọ̀yó ni bàtá à-jó-fẹ-eyín.

headword: Babaláwo kì í bèèrè ẹbọ àná.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The diviner does not ask for yesterday's sacrifice.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bẹbẹlúbẹ ò ì tíì débẹ̀; ibẹ̀ ló ń bọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The busybody is not there yet; but he is on his way.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá dàgbà à yé ogun-ún jà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "When one becomes old, one stops warring.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá fi inú wénú; iwọ là ń jẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If we compare notes with others, we wind up eating bile.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá ń bá ọmọdé jẹun lóko, gànmùganmu imú ẹni ní ń wò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one eats with a youth on the farm he stares at the protrusion of one's nose.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá ń gúnyán, kòmẹsẹ̀ á yọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one prepares pounded yams, the uninvited should depart.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá ti lè ṣe là ń wí; a kì í yan àna ẹni lódì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One admits to one's limits; one does not cease speaking to one's relatives-in-law.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá ti mọ là ń dé; a-láì-lẹ́ṣin kì í dé wọ̀nwọ̀n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One arrives according to one's worth; a horseless person does not arrive with the noise of hoofs and stirrups.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a bá ti mọ là ń kú; olongo kì í kú tìyàntìyàn.

headword: Bí a bá tọ̀ sílé, onípò a mọ ipò.

headword: Bí a bá wí pé ó dọwọ́ọ babaláwo, babaláwo a ló dọwọ́ Ifá; bí a bá ní ó dọwọ́ àgbà ìṣègùn, àgbà ìṣègùn a ló dọwọ́ Ọ̀sanyìn; bí a bá ní ó dọwọ́ ààfáà tó gbójú, a ní ó dọwọ́ Ọlọ́run ọ̀gá ògo.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one says that a matter now lies in the hands of the Ifá priest the Ifá priest says it lies in the hands of Ifá; if one says that it lies in the hands of the venerable medicine man the venerable medicine man says it rests in the hands of the god of herbs; if one says it rests in the hands of the formidable moslem priest he says it is in the hands of God the most glorious.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá dáṣọ lé aṣọ, a kì í pe ọ̀kan lákìísà.

headword: Bí a kò bá lọ sóko irọ́, a kì í pa á mọ́ni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one does not go to the farm of lies, lies are not told against one.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá ṣèké, a kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ́ kú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one has not been false, one does not die in disgrace.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá tíì jókòó, a kì í nasẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one has not yet sat down, one does not stretch one's legs out.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá tíì lè kọ́lé, àgọ́ là ń pa.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one is yet unable to build a house, one makes a tent.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá tó baba ọmọọ́ ṣe, a kì í pe alákàrà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one lacks the wherewithal to act like a father to a child, one does not summon the seller of bean fritters.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a kò bá tó ìyàá kọ̀ tí à ń kọ̀ ọ́, àjẹkún ìyà là ń jẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If one lacks the means to reject suffering and attempts to reject it, one's suffering simply multiplies.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí a ó ti tó kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà búburú; bí a ó ti mọ kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà rere.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The heights one will reach keeps one from evil deeds; the ordained limit to one's greatness keeps one from doing good deeds.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí àgbà kò bá ṣe ohun ẹ̀rù, ọmọdé kì í sá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If an elder does not do something fearful, the youth do not flee.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí àjànàkú ò bá rí ohun gbémì, kì í ṣe inú gbẹndu sọ́dẹ.

headword: Bí ajá rójú ẹkùn, a pa rọ́rọ́.

headword: Bí ayá bá mojú ọkọ, alárenà a yẹ̀bá.

headword: Bí ayé bá ń yẹni, ìwà ìbàjẹ́ là ń hù.

headword: Bí baálẹ̀ bá ń tàkìtì, òrógi là ń bá ẹmẹsẹ̀.

headword: Bí èèyán bá ní kò sí irú òun, àwọn ọlọgbọ́n a máa wòye.

headword: Bí eégbọn bá so mọ́ ajá lẹ́nu, akátá là ń ní kó já a?

headword: Bí ẹlẹ́bọ ò bá pe ẹni, àṣefín ò yẹni.

headword: Bí ìlàrí bá fẹ́ tẹ́, a ní kí lọba ó ṣe?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "When a courtier seeks disgrace, he asks, “What can the king do?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí iná bá dun ọbẹ̀, a dá ọ̀rọ̀ sọ.

headword: Bí mo bá torí oko kú n ó rò fáhéré; bí mo bá torí ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ kú n ó rò fódò; bí mo bá torí alábàjà òkíkí kú, n ó rò fóríì mi.

headword: Bí ó di ọdún mẹ́ta tí ẹkùn-ún ti ń ṣe òjòjò, olugbe la ó ha rán lọ bẹ̀ ẹ́ wò?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If it has been three years since the leopard took ill, is it a monkey that one sends to ask its condition?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí òfé ti ń fò la ti ń mọ̀ ọ́ lákọ ẹyẹ.

headword: Bí òkú fẹ̀, bí kò fẹ̀, ká bi ọmọ olókùú léèrè.

headword: Bí ojú bá rí, ẹnu a dákẹ́.

headword: Bí ojú kò bá ti olè, a ti ará ilé ẹ̀.

jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Even though the host's eyes are tiny, and the guest's eyes are huge, it is the host who holds sway over the guest.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí olóde ò kú, òdee rẹ̀ kì í hu gbẹ́gi.

headword: Bí ọdún bá dún, bọnnọnbọ́nnọ́n a pàwọ̀ dà.

jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "When the market disperses, only the head of the market women remains; only the venerable elders remain; when Ifá has had his say, the genius that consults him arises.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí ọjọ́ ewúrẹ́ bá pé, a ní kò sí ohun tí alápatà lè fi òun ṣe.

headword: Bí ọ̀lẹ́ ò lè jà, a lè kú tùẹ̀.

headword: Bí ọmọdé bá fẹ́ ṣìṣe àgbà, ọjọ́ oríi rẹ̀ ò níí jẹ́.

headword: Bí ọmọdé bá gun òkè àgbà, ó níláti gbọ́n.

headword: Bí ọmọdé bá ń ṣe ọmọdé, àgbà a máa ṣe bí àgbà.

headword: Bí ọmọdé ń lérí bébé, tí kò ní baba, ti baba là ń ṣe.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If a child brags a great deal, but has no father, one acts the part of a father.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Bí Ọya ń kọ lọ́run, bí Ṣàngó ń jó láyé, kò níí burú fún baba kó ní ó dọwọ́ ọmọ òun lọ́run.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Even if the goddess Ọya sings in heaven and the god Ṣango sings on earth, matters cannot be so bad for the father that he will say it is all up to his dead child in heaven.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Dìgbòlugi-dìgbòlùùyàn ò jẹ́ ká mọ ajá tòótọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The mad dog, and the person who behaves like a mad dog, both make it impossible for one to know the real dog.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Dídákẹ́ lerín dákẹ́; àjànàkú ló lẹgàn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The elephant has only chosen to remain silent; to the elephant belongs the forest.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Eégún ju eégún; òrìṣá ju òrìṣà; Pààká lé oníṣàngó wọ̀gbẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Some masqueraders are greater than others; some gods are greater than others; the masquerader Pààká chases the Ṣàngó worshipper into the bush.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Eégún ò na obìnrin lágọ̀; obìnrín tú kíjìpá ìdíi rẹ̀, ó fi na eégún.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The masquerader did not hit a woman with his shroud, but the woman unwraps her home-woven wrapper and hits the masquerader with it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Eégún pẹ́ lóde, ó fètè òkè dáhùn; wọ́n ní, “Baba kú àbọ̀,” ó ní, “Hì ìì.”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The masquerader stayed too long on parade and is reduced to speaking with his upper lip. headword: Eegun àjànàkú: ó há ìkokò lẹ́nu.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An elephant's bone: it sticks in the wolf's mouth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Eégbọn so mọ́ àyìnrín lẹ́nu, a ní kí adìẹ wá yán an jẹ; adìẹ́ mọ̀ pé òun náà oúnjẹ àyìnrín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A tick fastens on a fox's mouth and a chicken is asked to peck it off; the chicken, though, knows that it itself is food for a fox.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èmí dákọ okòó, ìwọ́ dákọ okòó, ò ń pèmí ní mùkọ-mùkọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "I bought twenty cowries worth of corn pap and you bought twenty cowries worth of corn pap, and you call me a corn pap addict.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èmi ìwọ̀fà, ìwọ ìwọ̀fà, o ní babá ní ká gbowó wá; o dá tìrẹ sílẹ̀ ná?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "I am a pawn, you are a pawn, and you tell me the creditor sent you to collect his money; have you repaid yours?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Epo ni mo rù; oníyangí má ba tèmi jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is palm oil that I am carrying; sandman, do not ruin my fortune.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Erin kì í fọn kọ́mọọ rẹ̀ ó fọn.

headword: Èrò ọ̀nà ni yó ròyìn ọkà tó gbó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is people who use the path that will spread the word about mature corn.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èsúrú ṣe fújà ó tẹ́ lọ́wọ́ oníyán; aláǹgbá ṣe fújà ó tẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ògiri; Ọlámọnrín àjàpá ṣe fújà ó tẹ́ lọ́wọ́-ọ̀ mi.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Èsúrú yam  forgets itself and loses favor with the maker of pounded yams; the lizard forgets itself and falls into disfavor with the wall; tortoise-like He-who-will-remain-nameless forgets himself and loses all regard with me.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Etí lobìnrín fi ń gbọ́ ohùn orò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is only with the ears that a woman hears the voice of Orò.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èwo ló tó ẹ̀kọọ́ gbà nínú ewé ìrúgbàá?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Which among the leaves of the locust-bean tree is adequate to receive corn-loaf?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ewújù tí yóò tú ọ̀pẹ: gbogbo eyín ẹ̀ ni yóò kán tán.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cane-rat that attempts to uproot a palm-tree will lose all its teeth in the attempt.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ewúrẹ́ ò wí pé òun ò ṣọmọ àgùntàn; àgùntàn ló wí pé òun ò ṣọmọ ewúrẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The goat did not say it was not sired by the sheep; it was the sheep that said it was not sired by the goat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ewúrẹ́ kì í bíni ká lọ sísọ̀ àgùntàn lọ jẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If sired by a goat, one does not go foraging in the realm of sheep.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èèyàn bí ọ̀bọ lọ̀bọ ń ya láṣọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Only people like monkeys have their clothing torn by monkeys.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Èèyàn ò ríbi sùn, ajá ń hanrun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Humans have no place to sleep, and a dog is snoring.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ẹ fà á wọlé” ló yẹ ẹlẹ́ṣin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“Lead it into the stable” is what becomes a horseman.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹ jẹ́ ká mí, ẹ jẹ́ ká simi; èèyàn ní ń fìdí èèyàn jókòó; èèyàn ìbá ṣe bí Ọlọ́run kò níí jẹ́ ká mí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Let us breathe, leave us in peace; the fashion is for people to sit on their behinds; were humans in the position of God they would not permit people to breathe.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ẹ kúulé” ò yẹ ará ilé; “Ẹ kú atìbà” ò yẹni tí ń tàjò bọ̀; ẹni tí ò kí ẹni, “Kú atìbà”-á pàdánù “Ẹ kúulé.”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“Greetings to you, house-bound ones” is improper for the house-bound to utter; “Welcome home” is not proper for the person arriving from a trip; whoever fails to give “welcome” to the person returning does himself or herself out of “greetings, house-bound.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹ̀bìtì ẹnu ò tàsé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The mouth-trap never misses.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹni là ń gúnyán ewùrà dè.

headword: Ẹ̀gbẹ̀rì ò mọ̀ pé arẹwà kì í gbé ẹ̀kú; gbogbo eyín kin-kìn-kin lábẹ́ aṣọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The novice does not know that a good-looking person does not wear a masquerade; all his perfectly white teeth are concealed beneath the cloth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹ̀gbọ́n ṣíwájú ó so aṣọ kọ́; àbúrò kẹ́yìn ó wẹ̀wù; bí a ò mọ̀lẹ, ọ̀lẹ ò mọ araa rẹ̀?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The elder walks in front, a loincloth draped over his shoulder; the younger walks behind, wearing a garment; if people cannot tell which one is shiftless, does he not know himself?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́ ń lọ ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́, o ní “Ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀ta ni àbí ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀fà?”; èwo lo gbé níbẹ̀?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person says he has lost an unspecified amount of money, and you ask if the amount is five hundred cowries or eleven hundred cowries; which amount did you steal?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ń pàfọ̀, ó rò pé òún ń ṣoge.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The pig wallows in mud, but thinks it is being a dandy.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ò mẹ̀yẹ.

headword: Ẹlẹ́ẹ́fà kì í lọ ẹẹ́fàa rẹ̀ ká sọ pé o di ìjẹfà tí a ti jẹun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "When a person proclaims the loss of six articles, one does not respond by saying one has not eaten in six days.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni à bá fi sóko kó dàparò, ó ní òun ẹni ilé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person one would leave on the farm hoping he would become a partridge boasts that he is the indispensable presence of the household.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowóo rẹ̀ ra àdá: ó ní ìyà àdá ń jẹ òun.

headword: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowóo rẹ̀ ra àtùpà: ó ní òun à-jí-tanná-wò-lóru.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who should be sold for money to purchase a lamp boasts that he is one-people-light-lamps-to-admire-at-night.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowóo rẹ̀ ra èbù: ó ní èlé òún kó ọ̀ọ́dúnrún.

headword: Ẹni à ń gbé gẹ̀gẹ̀ ni yó ba araa rẹ̀ jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the person who is revered that will disgrace himself or herself.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹní bá dẹ ojúu rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ á rímúu rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whoever gazes downwards with will see his or her nose.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹní dádé ti kúrò lọ́mọdé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person who wears a crown has outgrown childhood.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí a bá ń dáṣọ fún kì í ka èèwọ̀.

headword: Ẹni tí a fẹ́ yàtọ̀ sí ẹni tó ní kò sí irú òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person one loves is different from a person who says there is no one like him/herself.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí a gbé gun ẹlẹ́dẹ̀, ìwọ̀n ni kó yọ̀ mọ; ẹni tó gẹṣin, ilẹ̀ ló ń bọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person whom people have seated on a pig should moderate his or her strutting; even a horse rider will eventually come down to earth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí a lè gbé kì í dawọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who can be lifted does not hang limp.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí à ń wò láwò-sunkún ń wo araa rẹ̀ láwò-rẹ́rìn-ín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person whose appearance moves one to tears is moved to laughter by his own appearance.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí a ò fẹ́, àlọ́ ò kàn án.

headword: Ẹni tí a ò fẹ́ nílùú kì í jó lójú agbo.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person not welcome in the town does not take a turn in the dancing circle.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ipá ò hùwà ipá; ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ẹ̀lẹ̀ ò hu ẹ̀lẹ̀; ọ̀kùn tó nígba ọwọ́, tó nígba ẹsẹ̀ ń hùwà pẹ̀lẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person one would expect to be reckless is not reckless; the person one would expect to be cautious is not cautious; the millipede with two hundred arms and two hundred legs behaves very gently.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí kò lè gbé eèrà, tí ń kùsà sí erin, títẹ́ ní ń tẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who lacks the strength to lift an ant but rushes forward to lift an elephant ends in disgrace.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí kò rí ayé rí ní ń sọ pé kò sẹ́ni tó gbọ́n bí òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a person with limited experience of life who thinks there is none as wise as he.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tó tan araa rẹ̀ lòrìṣà òkè ń tàn: àpọ́n tí ò láya nílé, tó ní kí òrìṣà ó bùn un lọ́mọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the person who deceives himself that the gods above deceive: a bachelor who has no wife at home but implores the gods to grant him children.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tí kò tó gèlètè kì í mí fìn-ìn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who is not huge in stature does not breathe heavily.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ẹni tó tijú tì í fún araa rẹ̀.

headword: Ó tọ́ kí eégún léni lóko àgbàdo, èwo ni ti Pákọ̀kọ̀ láàrin ìlú?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It might be seemly for a masquerader to chase one off a corn farm, but it is not seemly for Pákọ̀kọ̀ to chase one in the middle of town.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó dínwó aró, kò yẹ atọ̀ọ́lé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is fitting for everybody to bargain to reduce the cost of dyeing clothes, but not the bed wetter.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó sọ pé “Ọlọ́run a-ṣèkan-má-kù,” kò yẹ akúkó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Everyone can justifiably say, “God, who has left nothing undone,” but not a eunuch.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odò kékeré lalákàn-án ti lè fọ́ epo; bó bá di àgàdàm̀gbá tán, odò a gbé alákàn lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is only in a small stream that the crab can make its oil; when it becomes huge and swift the river sweeps the crab away.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òfin ni yó sọ ara ẹ̀; ìyàwó tí ń na ọmọ ìyáálé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The law will assert itself, “as in the case of” a junior wife flogging the child of the senior wife.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogun tí olójú méjì rí sá ni olójú kan ní òún ń lọ jà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The war that the two-eyed person saw and fled is the same the one-eyed person vows he will join.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun méjì ló yẹ Ẹ̀ṣọ́: Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà, ó lé ogun; Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà ó kú sógun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Only two things are proper for a warrior: the warrior goes to war and drives the enemy off; the warrior goes to war and dies in battle.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí à ń tà là ń jẹ; kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ oní-kẹrosíìnì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "What one sells is what one eats; that does not apply to the kerosene seller.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí eèrá bá lè gbé ní ń pè ní ìgànnìkó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever the ant is able to carry is what it says is its full measure.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí ìrẹ̀ẹ́ ṣe tó fi kán lápá, aláàńtèté ní kí wọ́n jẹ́ kí òun ó ṣe è.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "That which the cricket attempted and broke a thigh, the aláàńtètè asks to be permitted to attempt.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí wèré fi ń s̩e ara ẹ̀, ó pọ̀ ju ohun tó fi ń ṣẹ ọmọ ẹlòmíràn lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "What the imbecile does to himself is far worse than what he does to others.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó ṣeé faga là ń faga sí; èwo ni,“Ìwòyí àná mo ti na ànaà mi fága-fàga”?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One boasts only about things proper to boast about; whoever heard of the boast, “By this time yesterday I had given my parent-in-law the beating of his life.”?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú àlejò la ti ń jẹ gbèsè; ẹ̀yìn-in ẹ̀ là ń san án.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is in a visitor's presence that one gets into debt; it is in her absence that one repays the debt.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú baba ara; awọ́n bí ojú; aṣòró dà bí àgbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The eye, father of the body; nothing is as valuable as the eye; nothing is as difficult to achieve as the status of elder.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú iná kọ́ lewùrà ń hurun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is not in the presence of the flame that water-yam grows hair.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́n ẹdun kó dẹni ilẹ̀; ìṣẹ́ kì í ṣẹ́ igún kó di ojúgbà adìẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The colobus monkey is never so reduced in circumstances that it becomes a land-hugging creature; the vulture is never so badly off that it becomes the equal of a chicken.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́n baálé ilé kó fọwọ́ gbálẹ̀ ilé ẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A head of a household is never so hard up that he sweeps his compound with his bare hands.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́n babaláwo kó bèèrè ẹbọ àná.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An Ifá diviner-priest is never so hard up that he asks for yesterday's sacrifice.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú ọ̀run kó ní kí ará ayé gba òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A dead person cannot be so desperate as to appeal to a living person for deliverance.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fàbúrò ẹni ṣaya.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One should not become so desperate that one takes one's younger sister as wife.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká pọ́n léyín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One's circumstances do not so deteriorate that one becomes red in teeth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú ò rọ́lá rí; ó bímọ ẹ̀ ó sọ ọ́ ní Ọláníyọnu.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person only newly acquainted with wealth; he has a son and names him Ọlaniyọnu.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú ò ti oníṣègùn, ó ní àna òun ń kú lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The medicine man lacks all shame, he announces that his parent-in-law is dying.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú ti agbọ́ń agbọ́n láfà kò léro.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Shame upon the wasp; the wasp has a nest but no honey.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òkété pẹ̀lú ọmọ ẹ̀ẹ́ di ọgbọọgba sínú ihò; nígba tí ìyá ń feyín pàkùrọ́, ọmọ náà ń feyín pa á pẹ̀lú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The giant bush rat and its child become equals in their hole; the mother cracks palm-nuts with its teeth, and the child does the same thing.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òkùnkùn ò mẹni ọ̀wọ̀; ó dÍfá fún “Ìwọ́ tá nìyẹn”?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Darkness does not know who deserves deference; it consulted the oracle Ifá for “Who might you be?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olómele kì í sọ pé igi yó dàá lóde lọ́la.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The omele drummer does not vow that there will be an earth-shaking performance on the morrow.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówó jẹun jẹ́jẹ́; òtòṣì jẹun tìpà-tìjàn; òtòṣì tí ń bá ọlọ́rọ̀ rìn, akọ ojú ló ń yá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The rich man eats slowly and at leisure; the poor person eats fast and with anxiety; the poor man who keeps company with a wealthy man is exceeding his station.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówó ní ń bá ọlọ́rọ̀ọ́ rìn; ẹgbẹ́ ní ń bá ẹgbẹ́ ṣeré.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a rich person that keeps company with a wealthy person; only people of equal standing play together.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówó ní ń jẹ iyán ẹgbàá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a rich person that eats pounded yams worth two thousand cowries.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òní, ẹtú jìnfìn, ọ̀la, ẹtú jìnfìn; ẹtu nìkan lẹran tó wà nígbó?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Today, the antelope falls into the ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is the antelope the only animal in the forest?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oníbàjẹ́ ò mọra; oníbàjẹ́ ń lọ sóko olè ó mú obìnrin lọ; ọkọ́ kó akọṣu, ìyàwó kó ewùrà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The shameless person does not know what is fitting; the shameless person is off to raid a farm, and he takes his wife along; the husband steals staple yams, the wife steals wateryams.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oníbàtá kì í wọ mọ́ṣáláṣí kó ní “Lèmámù ńkọ́?”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The bàtá drummer does not enter a mosque and ask “Where is the Imam?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onífunra àlejò tí ń tètè ṣe onílé pẹ̀lẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The excessively attentive visitor “who” extends hospitality greetings to the host.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; onílẹ̀kẹ̀ ìbá gbowo, ko rọ́rùn fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ so.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The person with goitre offers a ridiculously low price for beads; were the beads seller to accept her offer she would have no neck to string the beads around.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onílé ń jẹ èso gbìngbindò; alèjòó ní kí wọ́n ṣe òun lọ́wọ́ kan ẹ̀wà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The host is eating the fruits of the gbìngbindo tree; the visitor asks to be treated to some black-eyed peas.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: OníṢàngó tó jó tí kò gbọn yẹ̀rì: àbùkùu Ṣàngó kọ́; àbùkù ara ẹ̀ ni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The Ṣàngó worshipper who dances and does not shake his skirt: he does not disgrace Ṣàngó but himself.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: OníṢàngó tó jó tí kò tàpá, àbùkù ara ẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The Ṣàngó worshipper who dances and does nor kick his legs disgraces himself.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oníṣẹ̀ẹ́pẹ́-igí bímọ ó sọ ọ́ ní Ayọ̀-ọ́-kúnlé; ayọ̀ wo ló wà lára ìṣẹ́pẹ́ igi?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The seller of twigs for firewood has a child and names him Ayọ̀ọ́kúnle[Joy fills this home]; what sort of joy is to be found in firewood twigs?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oǹpè ní ń fa ọlá; òjípè kì í fa ọlá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the person who does the summoning that assumes airs; the person subject to summons does not assume airs.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orí àgbàá níyì, ó sàn ju orí àgbàá fọ́ lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The-elderly-person's-head-deserves-respect is better than The-elderly-person's-head-is-damaged.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orí awọ là ń bágbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is on the hide that one finds the elder.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oríi kí ní ń yá àpọ́n tó ń súfèé? Nítorí pé yó gùn-ún-yán fúnra ẹ̀ yó nìkan jẹ́?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "What is the cause of the bachelor's elation that makes him whistle? That he will make pounded yams for himself and eat it by himself?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orogún ìyá ẹ dáṣọ fún ọ ó ní kò balẹ̀; mélòó nìyá ẹ dá fún ọ tó fi kú?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Your mother's co-wife made a garment for you and you complain that it is not long enough; how many did your mother make for you before she died?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Òru ò molówó” nIfá tí à ń dá fún “Ìwọ ta nìyẹn?”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“The dark of night knows not who is a wealthy person” is the oracle one delivers to “Who might that be?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oòrùn, kó tìẹ wọ̀ ká má bàá Ọlọ́jọ́ wí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Sun, go set so one does not blame the owner of the day.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òtòlòó jẹ, òtòlòó mu, òtòlòó fẹsẹ̀ wé ẹsẹ̀ erin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The water-buck ate, the water-buck drank, the water-buck compared its limbs to an elephant's.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oúnjẹ ọmọ kékeré a máa wọ àgbà nínú; òrùka ọmọ kékeré ni kì í wọ ágbá lọ́wọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A youth's food can enter the stomach of an elder; it is only a youth's ring that cannot slip unto an elder's finger.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó ẹ̀yẹ ò sú ẹnií san; tọ̀ràn ni ò súnwọ̀n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "People have no difficulty paying the money for glorious events; it is the money for trouble that is unpleasant to pay.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọbẹ̀ kì í gbé inú àgbà mì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A stew does not slush around once inside an elder.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀bún ríkú ọkọ tìrànmọ́; ó ní ọjọ́ tí ọkọ òún ti kú òun ò fi omi kan ara.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The filthy person takes advantage of her husband's death for blame; she says since her husband died she has not violated her person with water.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀gà-ǹ-gà lọmọọ̀ mi ń jẹ́, ẹ má pe ọmọọ̀ mi ní Ògò-ǹ-gò mọ́! Èwo lorúkọ rere níbẹ̀?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "My child's name is Ọ̀gàǹgà; don't you call my child Ògòǹgò any more! Which of the two is a good name.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀gẹ̀gẹ́ ò lẹ́wà; lásán ló fara wéṣu.

headword: Ọmọdé dáwọ́tilẹ̀, ó ní òún tó ọ̀bọ; bó tó ọ̀bọ, ó tó gẹ̀gẹ̀ àyàa ẹ̀?

headword: Ọ̀ṣìn ò lè mú àwòdì òkè; Bámidélé lọ̀ṣín lè mú.

headword: O rojọ́ láàárọ̀ o ò jàre, ó dalẹ́ o ní kọ́ba dúró gbọ́ tẹnu ẹ; ohun tó o wí láàárọ̀ náà kọ́ lo máa wí lálẹ́?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You state your case in the morning and you are not vindicated, and at nightfall you plead with the king to delay a bit and listen to what you have to say; isn't what you have to say in the evening the same thing you said in the morning?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: O sá fún ikú, o bọ́ sí àkọ̀ idà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You run from death and seek refuge in a scabbard.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ó ṣe mí rí”; ògbó adìẹẹ́ rí àwòdì sá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“I have experienced it before”; a grown chicken flees at the sight of a kite.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó ti ojú orun wá ó ń fọ ẹnà; ó ní “ẹ jẹ́ ká máa ji ní mẹ́mu-mẹ́mu.”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "He woke up from sleep and spoke in scrambled language; he said, “Let us wake it in moos.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: O wà láyé, mo wà láàyè, ò ń bi mí bí ọ̀rún ṣe rí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You are on earth “alive” and I am on earth, and yet you ask me what heaven is like.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó yẹ kí eégún mọ ẹni tó mú àgbò so.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is proper that the masquerader know who tethered the ram.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Obìnrin ò gbé ibi tó máa rọ̀ ọ́ lọ́rùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A woman never remains where her well being rests.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òbò ò ṣé ṣe àlejò.

headword: Odídẹrẹ́ dawo, ìkó ìdí ẹ̀ẹ́ dọ̀gbẹ̀rì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The parrot becomes fully initiated into the secrets, his tail feather becomes a non-initiate.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odó iyán ò jẹ́ gún ẹ̀lú; odó ẹ̀lú ò jẹ́ gúnyán; àtẹ táa fi ń pàtẹ ìlẹ̀kẹ̀, a ò jẹ́ fi pàtẹ ọ̀rúnlá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The mortar used for pounding yams will not do for pounding indigo leaves; the mortar for pounding indigo leaves will not do for yams; the tray on which beads are displayed for sale will not do for displaying dried okro.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òdú kì í ṣe àìmọ̀ olóko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The òdú vegetable is not something the farmer does not know.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogún kì í pọ̀ ká pín fún aládùúgbò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The inheritance is never so abundant that one shares it with neighbors.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogún ń bókòó? Òwe aṣiwèrè.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Twenty or a score? An imbecile's puzzle.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohùn àgbà: bí kò ta ìgún, a ta èbù.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An elder's voice: if it does not yield yams ready for pounding (for food), it will yield yam seedlings ready for planting.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a bá pàdé ò jọ ohun tí a rí tẹ́lẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "That which one comes upon is nothing to compare to what one has always had.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a ni la fi ń kẹ́ ọmọ ẹni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is what one has that one uses to spoil one's child.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a ò rí rí lèèwọ̀ ojú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is something one has never seen before that is taboo for the eyes.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a ṣe nílé àna ẹni, “Ojú ń tì mí” kúrò níbẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "What one does in the home of one's parents-in-law leaves no room for “I am bashful.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ káṣọ pé méjì ni ò jẹ́ kó dú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The same thing that keeps one from having more than one item of clothing also keeps that one from blackening from dirt.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ kí oko pọ̀ ni ò jẹ́ kó mọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever limits the size of a farm is the same thing that makes it overgrown with weeds.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó fọ́ni lójú ló ń júwe ọ̀nà fúnni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever deprives one of one's sight is the same thing that shows one the way.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó jọ oun la fi ń wé ohun; èpo ẹ̀pà ló jọ ìtẹ́ ẹ̀lírí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is what resembles a thing that one compares it with; peanut shells are most like the nest of the rodent ẹ̀lírí.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó ní òun óò bẹ́ni lórí, bó bá ṣíni ní fìlà, ká dúpẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If a thing that vows to decapitate one only knocks off one's hat, one shounld be thankful.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó ní òun óò ṣeni lẹ́rú, tó wá ṣeni níwọ̀fà, ká gbà á.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If whatever promised to make one a slave only makes one a pawn, one should accept one's fate.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun-a-lè-ṣe, tó forí sọ àpò òwú; wọ́n ní ṣe bó rí yangí nílẹ̀, ó ní “Ohun a bá lè ṣe là ń lérí sí.”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Ohunalese who dashes his head against a sack of cotton wool; people asked if he did not see the rock nearby; he replied, “One should vow to do only what one can safely accomplish.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òjò ò ì dá a ní kò tó tàná.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It has not yet stopped raining and some observe that today's rainfall is not as much as yesterday's.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òjòwú ò já gèlè; kooro ló lè já.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The jealous woman does not snatch her head gear off; all she can do is threaten a fight.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òjòwú ò lẹ́ran láyà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The jealous woman lacks flesh on her chest.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú àwo làwó fi ń gba ọbẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is on its face that a plate accepts soup.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kan làdá ń ní.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A cutlass has only one edge.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fi pọ́nlẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One should not because of one's suffering try honing one's eyes on the ground.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká mu ìṣápá; òùngbẹ kì í gbẹni ká mu ẹ̀jẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One is never so desperate that one drinks red sorrel juice; one is never so thirsty that one drinks blood.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í ti àgbà lóru; jagun a lóṣòó góńgó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An elderly person does not become embarrassed under cover of darkness; the stalwart squats nonchalantly.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú kì í ti eégún kó má mọ̀nà ìgbàlẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A masquerader is never so shamed that he cannot find his way to the secret grove.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú la fi ḿmọ àísí epo; ẹnu la fi ń mọ àìsíyọ̀; ọbẹ̀ tí ò bá lépo nínú òkèèrè la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is with the eyes that one tells the absence of palm-oil; it is with the mouth that one determines the absence of salt; if a stew lacks oil, it is the eyes that will tell.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ojú tó rọ̀ nirorẹ́ ń sọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Pimples attack only faces that are delicate.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Òkè ìhín ò jẹ́ ká rí tọ̀ún” ò ṣéé pa lówe nílé àna ẹni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“The nearer hill kept one from seeing the farther one” is not a proverb one uses in one's parents-in-law's home.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Okó ilé kì í jọ obìnrin lójú, àfi bó bá dó tìta.

headword: Oko kì í jẹ́ ti baba àti tọmọ kó má nìí àlà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Farms do not, by virtue of belonging to a father and his son, lack boundaries.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oko mímọ́ ṣeé ro; ọ̀nà mímọ́ dùn-ún tọ̀; gbogbo ìyàwó dùn-ún gbàbálé; aṣọ ìgbàá ṣeé yọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A clean farm is a pleasure to weed; a clean-swept path is a pleasure to trod; all new wives are a pleasure to deflower; the new fashionable cloth of the season is a pleasure to wear.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Okotoroboó tùyẹ́ sílẹ̀ ọmọ titún ń gbe jó; ó ní ó rọ òun lọ́rùn lòún tu ú?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Okotorobo, a bird, casts away a feather, and a young chick picks it up to dance with it; the one who shed the feathers asks, would I have discarded it if it was not a nuisance.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Okotoroboó yé ẹyin sílẹ̀, àdàbà ń garùn wo ẹyin ẹlẹ́yin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Okotorobo the bird lays an egg, and the turtle dove stretches its neck to inspect the egg that does not belong to it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òkú ẹran kì í ti ajá lójú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A dog is never to squeamish to eat a carcase.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olè tó gbé fèrè ọba ò róhun gbé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The thief who stole the king's bugle could find nothing to steal.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olé tó jí kàkàkí, níbo ni yó ti fọn ọ́n?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A thief who stole a bugle, where will he blow it?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olóògùn ní ńṣe bí a-láigbọ́-mọ̀ràn; bí ogun ó bàá wọ̀lú ọlọgbọ́n là ńfọ̀rọ̀ lọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The medicine man behaves like a person impervious to wise counsel; if war threatens a town the person to consult for counsel is the sage.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olóhun-ún dolè; “Gbà bù jẹ́” dolóhun.

headword: Olóhun kì í rí ohun ẹ̀ kó pè é lórò.
