headword: Olórìṣà tó da kiriyó: ọjọ́ tó gbọ́ dùrù orí ijó lẹsẹ̀ẹ́ kán sí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The idol worshipper who became a Christian; the day he first heard the organ play he lost his legs dancing.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olòṣì ọmọ ní ń fọwọ́ òṣì júwe ilée babaa ẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a worthless child that points the way to his father's house with his left-hand fingers.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olóúnjẹẹ́ tóó bá kú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Someone who has food is worth dying with.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówe laláṣẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who knows proverbs has the last word in a dispute.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówó á wá; aláwìn á wá; ìlú tí à ń gbé la gbé ń gbàwìn; à-rà-àì-san ni ò súnwọ̀n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Those who have money will come, and those who will buy on credit will come; it is in one's town that one buys on credit; failure to eventually pay up is what is bad.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Olówó pèlù o ò jó; ọjọ́ wo lo máa rówó pe tìẹ?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A rich person engages a dance band and you do not dance; when will you have the money to hire your own band?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òmùgọ̀ èèyàn ní ń bóbìnrin mulẹ̀: ọjọ́ tóbìnrín bá mawo lawó bàjẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A rich person engages a dance band and you do not dance; when will you have the money to hire your own band?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òmùgọ̀ ní ń gbé ígunnu; ọlọgbọ́n ní ń gbowó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the fool that wears the Nupe masquerade; it is the wise person that collects the monetary gifts.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onígi ní ń figi ẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the firewood seller who sets a low price for his wares.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onígbá ní ń pe igbá ẹ̀ ní àíkàrágbá káyé tó fi kólẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the owner of the calabash who first called it a broken piece of gourd before the world used it for scooping dirt.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onígbèsè tí ń pa àpatà ẹyẹ́lé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Habitual debtor who butchers a pigeon for sale.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; adámú fi sàárà san ẹgbẹ̀ta.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The goitered person sets a low price on beads; the person with a blocked nose repays six thousand cowries with alms.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oníṣègùn tó sọ pé díẹ̀ ò tó òun, òfo ni yó fọwọ́ mú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The medicine man who is dissatisfied with a modest payment will wind up with nothing.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ooré pẹ́, aṣiwèrèé gbàgbé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The favor is long past; the imbecile forgets.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orí ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ popo láwo; bí a wí fọ́mọ ẹni a gbọ́ràn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The squirrel's head sits in a plate like a lump; if one counsels one's child it should listen.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orí tí yó jẹ igún kì í gbọ́; bí wọ́n fun ládìẹ kò níí gbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The head that is destined to eat a vulture cannot be saved; if a chicken is offered to it it will refuse.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orí tó kọ ẹrù, owó ní ńnáni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A head that refuses “to carry” loads will cost its owner some money.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orin tí ò ṣoroó dá kì í ṣòroó gbè; bí ó bá ní “héééé,” à ní “háááá.”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A song that is not difficult to lead is not difficult to follow; if the leader sings “haaaay,” one responds “haaaah.”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Orín yí, ìlùú yí padà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The song changes, and the drumming changes to suit.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òrìṣà tó ní tÒgún kì í ṣe ọ̀nà ò ní rí nńkan jẹ lásìkò tó fẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The god that says matters pertaining to Ògún are irrelevant will not find anything to eat when he/she wishes.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oòrùn kì í jẹ iṣu àgbà kó má mọbẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An elder does not lose his yams to the sun without knowing where the event happened.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oòrùn kì í là kínú bí olóko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The sun does not shine and cause displeasure in the farmer.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òṣùpá lé a ní kò gún; ẹni tọ́wọ́ ẹ̀ ẹ́ bá to kó tún un ṣe.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The moon appears and people say it is not straight; whoever can reach it let him go and right it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òtòṣì ò gbọ́ tìṣẹ́ ẹ̀ ó ní ogún kó àparò; ọdẹ́ rorò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The destitute person does not look to repairing his fortune; he says the partidge has been captured in a war, for the hunter is merciless.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó kì í lóye kọ́mọ kú sẹ́rú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If the amount of money is known, a child cannot die in slavery.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó kì í yéye kọ́mọ ó kú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If money is available in abundance, a child does not die.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó la fi ń fíná owó; bí ẹgbẹ̀rún bá so lókè, igbió la fi ń ká a.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Money is what one uses to kindle the fire for money; if a thousand cowries grow from the branches above, one uses two hundred cowries to pluck them.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó la fi ń lògbà; ọgbọ́n la fi ń gbélé ayé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is with money that we secure pleasures; it is with wisdom that one secures a good life.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó ní ń pa ọjà ọ̀mọ̀ràn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is money that brings a knowing person's trading to a conclusion.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owó tọ́mọdé bá kọ́kọ́ ní, àkàrà ní ń fií rà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The first money a youth comes into he spends on bean fritters.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òwú kì í là kínú bí olóko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cotton seed does not open and thus anger the farmer.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Owú pani ju kùmọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Jealousy kills more surely than a cudgel.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òyìnbó Òkè Eléérú, ó ṣubú sóde Alọ́ba; kùmọ̀ ni yó gbe dìde.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The white man from Òkè Elérú; he collapses in front of Alọba's compound; cudgels will help him up.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀bẹ ń wólé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ń ba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The knife is destroying its own home, it says it is ruining the sheath.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọbẹ̀ tí baálé kì í jẹ, ìyáálé ilé kì í sè é.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The sort of stew the man of the house will not eat, the woman of the house should not cook.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀dẹ̀ ọmọ ń fi ìdò ṣeré.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An idiot child that plays with ìdò flowers.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ ò gba òró, àfi abẹ́ ọdán.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The porch does not accommodate standing people; only the shade of the (ọdán) banyan tree does.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀fàfà fohùn ṣakin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The tree-bear wins renown with its voice.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n a-dákọ-kéré ò tó ti a-yọwó-má-rà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cunning of the person who skimps on the measure of her corn meal is not as great as that of the would-be purchaser who refuses to buy.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n dùn-ún gbọ́n; ìmọ́ dùn-ún mọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Wisdom is a good thing to have; knowledge is a good thing to have.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n ju agbára.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Wisdom is greater than strength.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n kì í tán.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Wisdom is never used up.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọn la fi ń gbé ayé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One needs wisdom to live in this world.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n lajá fi ń pa ìkokò bọ Ifá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is cunning that the dog employs in order to sacrifice a wolf to Ifá.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n ní ń ṣẹgun; ìmọ̀ràn ní ń ṣẹ́ ẹ̀tẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Cunning wins battles; knowledge defeats plots.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n la fi ń ṣọgbọ́n, ìmọ̀ràn ẹnìkan ò tọ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One learns wisdom from other people's wisdom one person's knowledge does not amount to anything.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n tí ahún gbọ́n, ẹ̀yìn ni yó máa tọ ti ìgbín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cunning that the tortoise has will always rank behind that of the snail.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n tí ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi pa ẹfọ̀n ló fi ń jẹ ẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The same cunning with which the toad killed the buffalo will show it how to eat the prey.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọọgbọ́n làgbàlagbàá fi ń sá fún ẹran ńlá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is with cunning that a grown man runs away from a bull.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọjọ́ eré là ń jiyàn ohun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is on a playful occasion that one argues about matters.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọjọ́ tíìlùú bá ń lu onílù, iṣẹ́ mìíràn-án yá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The day the drum begins to beat the drummer is the day he should seek another employment.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọjọ́ tí olówó ń ṣẹbọ ni à-wà-jẹ-wà-mu ìwọ̀fà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The day the person who did the hiring makes a sacrifice is the day the hired hand eats and drinks.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ ń sunkún agbádá; èyí tí àjàòó dá léṣìí kí ló fi ṣe? Ṣebí igi ló fi n gùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The squirrel weeps for want of a stately garment; the garment the àjàò bird made last year, what did it do with it? Was it not tree climbing it used the garment for?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọkọ́ ọlọ́kọ́ la fi ń gbọ́n èkìtì.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is other people's hoe that one uses to clear a mound of rubbish.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ń yọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One at a time is how one extricates one's feet from a mire.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ń yọ ẹsẹ̀ lẹ́kù.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One at a time is how one removes one's legs from a masquerade costume.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọkùnrin jẹ́jẹ́ a-bìwà-kunkun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An easy-going man's gentle mien hides a strong disposition.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọ ò lọ ló dé Ìbarà? Ìbarà a máa ṣe ilé ọlọ?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "If the grindstone did not move, how did it get to Ìbarà? Is Ìbarà the home of grindstones?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọ́gbọ́n jẹni bí ẹmùrẹ́n; aṣiwèré jẹni bí ìgbọ̀ngbọ̀n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The wise person bites one like a mosquito; the mad person bites one like a gadfly.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọgbọ́n ló lè mọ àdììtú èdè.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Only a wise person can decipher the meaning of speech.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọgbọ́n ń dẹ ihò, ọ̀mọ̀ràn-án dúró tì í; ọlọgbọ́n ní “Háà, ó jáde!”Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Háà, mo kì í!”Ọlọgbọ́n ní “Kí lo kì?” Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Kí nìwọ náà-á ló jáde?”
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cunning man is watching a hole, and the knowledgeable person is standing by him; the cunning man exclaims, “Ha, it has sprung out!” The knowledgeable person responds, “Ha, I have grabbed it!” The cunning person asks, “What did you grab?” The knowledgeable person asks in turn, “What did you say sprang out?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọgbọ́n ni yó jogún ògo; aṣiwèrè ni yó ru ìtìjú wálé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The wise child will inherit glory; the idiot child will bring shame home with him.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọgbọ́n ọmọ ní ń mú inúu bàbá ẹ̀ dùn; aṣiwèrè ọmọ ní ń ba inú ìyá ẹ̀ jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A wise child gladdens the heart of his father; an imbecile of a child saddens the heart of his mother.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọ́jà kì í wí pé kọ́jà ó tú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The owner of the market never wishes the market to be disrupted.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọ́tí kì í mọ ọmọ ẹ̀ lólè
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The wine seller never realizes that his child is a thief.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọlọ́tọ̀ọ́ ní tòun ọ̀tọ̀; ìyá ẹ̀ẹ́ kú nílé, o gbé e lọ sin sóko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Ọlọ́tọ̀ says his ways are different; his mother dies at home and he takes her to the farm for burial.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ atiro tó ra bàtà fún bàbá ẹ̀, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ gbọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The child of a cripple who bought shoes for his father is asking for a stern lecture.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ ẹní dàra, bíi ká fi ṣaya kọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One's child may be beautiful, but one cannot make her one's wife.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹni ò jọ ọmọ ẹni; ọmọ eni ìbá jiyán, ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹ́ni a jẹ̀kọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Other people's children are not like one's own; when one's child eats pounded yams, other people's children will eat corn meal loaf.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ ẹni kì í gbọnsẹ̀ ká fi eèsún nù ú nídìí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One does not, after one's child defecates, wipe the child's anus with the abrasive elephant grass.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ iná là ń rán síná.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is the child of fire that one sends on an errand to fire.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ọmọọ̀ mi ò yó” la mọ̀; “ọmọọ̀ mí yó, ṣùgbọ́n kò rí sáárá fẹ́,” a ò mọ ìyẹn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“My child did not have enough to eat,” we understand; “My child had enough to eat but had no snuff to snort,” that we do not understand.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọ tí ò ní baba kì í jìjà ẹ̀bi.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A fatherless child should not engage in an unjust fight.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé kékeré ò mọ ogun, ó ní kógun ó wá, ó ní bógún bá dé òun a kó síyàrá ìyá òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A small child does not know what war is like, hence, he says that war should break out, for when it does he will go hide in his mother's room.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé kì í mọ àkókò tí kúrò-kúròó fi ń kúrò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A small child never knows when kúròkúrò takes its leave.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọde kì í mọ ìtàn, kó mọ à-gbọ́-wí, kó mọ ọjọ́ tí a ṣe ẹ̀dá òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child does not know so much history and know so much hearsay that it knows the day of its creation.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé kì í mọ orií jẹ kó má rá a lẹ́nu.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child is never so careful about eating corn meal that it does not smear the meal on its mouth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé kì í ní ina níle kí tòde má jòó o.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child does not have fire at home and therefore escape being burned by the fire abroad.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé mọ sáárá, ṣùgbọ́n kò mọ àlọ̀yí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child knows snuff, but does not know how to grind and turn the tobacco.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé ní wọ́n ńjẹ igún, bàbá ẹ̀ẹ́ ní wọn kì í jẹ ẹ́; ó ní ẹnìkán jẹ ẹ́ rí lójú òun; bàbá ẹ̀ẹ́ ní ta ni? Ó ní ẹni náà ò sí.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child says that people do eat vultures, and its father says people do not; the child says someone did eat a vulture in its presence; its father asks, who? The child says the person is dead.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé ò mẹ̀fọ́, ó ń pè é légbògi.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child does not recognize a vegetable and calls it medicine.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé ò mọ oògùn, ó ń pè é lẹ́fọ̀o?; kò mọ̀ pé ikú tó pa baba òun ni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child does not know medicine and he therefore calls it vegetables; it does not recognize it as what killed its father.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé ò moògùn ó ń pè é lẹ́gùn-ún.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A child does not know medicine and says it is a thorn.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọmọdé yìí, máa wò mí lójú, ẹni (tí) a bá lọ sóde là ń wò lójú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Child, keep your eyes on me; one keeps one's eyes on the person who takes one visiting.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀mọ̀ràn ní ń mọ oyún ìgbín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Only a sage knows the pregnancy of a snail.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pá gbóńgbó ní n ṣíwájú agbọ́ọni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a small walking-stick that goes before the person who walks a path overhung with foliage that is wet with morning dew.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọpẹ́ ló yẹ ẹrú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Gratitude is what befits the slave.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ èèyàn, bí a ò bá gbé e lulẹ̀, kò níí lè fọhùn ire.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person who is like the divining string: unless you throw him down he will not talk sense.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní kéjò máa kálọ; ìjà òún di ojú ọ̀nà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The toad tells the snake to follow it, for it does not fight except by the roadside.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní òún lè sín ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; ta ní jẹ́ fi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sídìí ọmọọ ẹ̀?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The toad boasts that it knows how to string beads; who, though, would put a toad's beads around his child's waist?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀ ń yan káńdú-kàǹdù-káńdú lóju ẹlẹ́gùúsí; ẹlẹ́gùúsí ò gbọdọ̀ yí i lata.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The toad struts nonchalantly before the person cooking ẹ̀gúsí stew; the person cooking the ẹ̀gúsí stew will never add it to the ingredients.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò mọ̀nà odò, ó dà á sí àwàdà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The toad does not know the way to the stream and turns matters into a jest.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ òjò ní ń lé eégún wọlé kẹri-kẹri.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a deluge that chases the eégún masquerader indoors indefinitely.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀ràn kan la fi ń ṣòfin ọ̀kan.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One problem serves as the basis for a law that will apply to another case.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀ràn ọlọ́ràn la fi ń kọ́gbọ́n.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "From other people's problems one learns wisdom.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀ràn tí ò sunwọ̀n, konko ǹ ṣojú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A matter that is unpalatable hardens the eyes.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ kì í gbórín ká fi ọ̀bẹ bù ú, ẹnu la fi ń wí i.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A problem is not so formidable that one attacks it with a knife; one tackles it with the mouth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ la fi ń jẹ omitooro ọ̀rọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Words are the things with which to savor the delicious broth of words.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ọ́ ni òun ò nílé; ibi tí wọ́n bá rí ni wọ́n ti ń sọ òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Discourse says it has no home; people engage in it wherever they please.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ rere ní ń yọ obì lápò; ọ̀rọ̀ búburú ní ń yọ ọfà lápó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Good talk brings the kola-nut out of the pouch; provocative talk draws the arrow out of th quiver.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ọlọgbọ́n bá sọ, ẹnu aṣiwèrè la ti ń gbọ́ ọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever a wiseman says will be heard repeated by the nitwit.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀rọ̀ tó dojú rú di ti ọlọ́rọ̀, ayé á dẹ̀yìn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A problem that is too complicated to resolve becomes the sole responsibility of the person concerned; the world leaves him/her to his/her devices.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọsán gbé ojú ọrun le kókó; bó bá wọ odò, a di ọ̀-rọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The bow-string is taut while it remains on the bow; dipped into the river it becomes very soft indeed.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀sán ọ̀run ò pọ́n; ẹni tó bá yá kó máa bá tiẹ̀ lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is not yet noon time in heaven; whoever is anxious to get there may go ahead by himself/herself.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọwọ́ aṣiwèrè ni a gbé ń bá apá yíya.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is in the hands of an imbecile that one finds a severed arm.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀wọ̀ọ kókó la fi ń wọ igi; ọ̀wọ̀ òrìṣà la fi ń wọ àfín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The regard one has for the knob is the one with which one clothes the tree; the regard one has for the gods is the same that one invests the albino with.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Rà á ire, gà á ire; ìpéǹpéjú ni àlàa fìlà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Press it well on the head; puff it out; the eyebrow is the limit for the cap.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ràdà-ràdà-á mọ ibi tí ó ńrè.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The meandering person knows where he is headed.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Rírí tí a rí igún la fi ń ta igún lọ́fà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is because one sees the vulture that one shoots arrows at it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Sìn mí ká relé àna,” ó wẹ̀wù ẹtù.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“Go with me to my in-laws' home,” and he wore a garment made from rich hand-woven material.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Sọ̀rọ̀ kí ọlọ́rọ̀ gbọ́, àbùkù ní ń fi kanni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Spreading rumors into the ears of the subject of the rumor brings disgrace to one.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ṣàǹgó kì í jà kó mú ilé aró.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Ṣango does not fight and destroy the enclosure for dyeing.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ṣàngó ní òun ní ń kó ọkùnrin suuru bá jà; Èṣù ní bíi tòun? Ṣàngó ní kí tÈṣù kúrò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Ṣàngó says he gathers people around him to fight together; Èṣù asks if Ṣàngó includes people like him, and Ṣàngó says Èṣù is the exception.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ṣe mí níṣu” ní ń ṣíwájú “ẹ kúuṣẹ́” bí?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Does “Give me some yam” go before “Hello there, you working man.”?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ṣẹ̀kẹ̀rẹ̀ ò ṣéé fọ̀pá na.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The beaded musical gourd is not something to play with a stick.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ṣẹ́kẹ́ṣẹkẹ̀ dára, ṣùgbọ́n alágbẹ̀dẹ ò rọ ọ́ fún ọmọ ẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Handcuffs are pretty, but the blacksmith does not fashion them for his own child.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Sútà ò nílé; ìkóríta lÈṣù ń gbé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Perfidy has no home; the home of Èṣù is the crossroads.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ta lèèyàn nínú ẹrú Ààrẹ? A ní Ìdaganna la wá wá, ẹ ní Ìdakolo?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Which of the Ààrẹ́'s slaves is a person of any account? We said we came looking for Ìdaganna, and you ask, “Ìdakolo?”", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ta ní jẹ́ jẹ ọṣẹ kó fògìrì fọṣọ?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Who would eat soap and wash clothes with fermented beans?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ta ní mọ̀dí òjò, bí kò ṣe Ṣàngó?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Who can know the secret of the rain if not Ṣàngo?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Tábà tí ò dùn, ẹnu ò tà á.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Snuff that is not pleasant, the mouth cannot not sell.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Tèmi ò ṣòro,” tí kì í jẹ kọ́mọ alágbẹ̀dẹ ní idà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“Mine is not urgent.” which prevents the son of the blacksmith from owning a sword.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Onínúfùfù ní ń wá oúnjẹ fún onínúwẹ́rẹ́wẹ́rẹ́.

headword: Oore ọ̀fẹ́ gùn jùwàásù.

headword: Oore tí igúnnugún ṣe tó fi pá lórí, tí àkàlá ṣe tó fi yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀, a kì í ṣe irú ẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The sort of favor the vulture did and went bald, the sort of favor the ground hornbill did and developed a goitre, one does not do it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ooreé pọ̀, a fìkà san án.

headword: Òòrẹ̀ ní ń ṣẹ́gi tí a ó fi wì í.

headword: Orí ejò ò ṣéé họ imú.

headword: Òrìṣà kékeré ò ṣéé há ní párá.

headword: Oúnjẹ tí a ó jẹ pẹ́, a kì í bu òkèlèe ẹ̀ tóbi.

headword: Ọ̀bánijà ní ń mọ ìjagun ẹni.

headword: Ọbẹ ṣìlòó ń báni ṣeré a ní kò mú; bí eré bí eré ó ń pani lọ́wọ́.

headword: Ọbẹ̀ tóo sè tílé fi jóná wàá sọ ọ́.

headword: Ọ̀gán ìmàdò ò ṣéé kò lójú.

headword: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ń bàjẹ́, a ní ó ń pọ́n.

headword: Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù ní ń pa òdù ọ̀yà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is excessive cunning that kills the mature cane rat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Excessive cleverness turns one into a phantom; if there is too much magical charm it turns the owner into an imbecile; if a woman is too cunning her husband's clothes wind up ill-fitting.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọgbọ́n ọdúnnìí, wèrè ẹ̀míì.

headword: Ọgbọ́n pẹ̀lúu sùúrù la fi ń mú erin wọ̀lú.

headword: Ọjọ́ tí a ó bàá nù, gágá lara ń yáni.

headword: Ọjọ́ tí a to ọkà a ò to ti èkúté mọ́ ọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The day one arranged one's corn in the granary, one did not think in terms of the rat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọjọ́ tí àgbẹ̀ ṣíṣeé bá di kíyèsílẹ̀, ká ṣíwọ́ oko ríro.

headword: Ọjọ́ tí elétutuú bá máa fò, ìjàm̀pere kì í rìn.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà àgbẹ̀ tí ń gbin òwú sóko àkùrọ̀.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba àrùn.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba olè; àwòròǹṣoṣòó wo ohun olóhun má ṣèẹ́jú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Covetousness, father of thievery; bug-eyed greedy person stares at another person's property without blinking.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwàá bu òkèlè, ojù ẹ̀ẹ́ lami.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà èèyàn-án dé àwùjọ, ó wòkè yàn-yàn-àn-yàn.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà kì í mu ẹ̀jẹ̀ ẹlòmíràn; ẹ̀jẹ̀ ara ẹ̀ náà ní ń mu.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The greedy person does not drink other people's blood; he drinks only his own.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà ò ṣéé fi wá nǹkan.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà ológbò tó jókòó sẹ́nu ọ̀nà; ṣé eku eléku ló fẹ́ pa jẹ?

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà Oníṣàngó ní ń sọ ọmọ rẹ̀ ní Bámgbóṣé; ìwọ̀n oṣé tí a lè gbé là ń gbé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is an insatiable Ṣàngó priest who names his son Bámigbóṣé one should procure for oneself a ritual rod one can carry.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwà pẹ̀lú olè, déédé ni wọ́n jẹ́.

headword: Ọ̀kánjúwàá pín ẹgbàafà nínú ẹgbàaje; ó ní kí wọ́n pín ẹgbàá kan tó kù, bóyá igbiwó tún lè kan òun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The insatiable person receives twelve thousand cowries out fourteen thousand; he asked that the remaining two thousand be shared, perhaps two hundred of them will come to him.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ gorí ìrókò, ojú ọdẹẹ́ dá.

headword: Kò sí ẹni tí Ọlọ́run ò ṣe fún, àfi ẹni tó bá ní tòun ò tó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is no one to whom God has not been generous, only those who will say he has not been generous enough.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kò sí ibi tí kò gba ọ̀gọ̀; ọ̀lẹ layé ò gbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is no place where a fool is not welcome; the world rejects only shiftless people.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kò sí ibi tí ọwọ́-ọ̀jà erin ò tó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is no place an elephant's trunk cannot reach.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kò sí ikú tí kò rọ adìẹ lọ́rùn.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is no manner of death that is inconvenient for the chicken.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kò sí ohun tí ń ti òkè bọ̀ tí ilẹ̀ ò gbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is nothing dropping from above that the earth cannot withstand.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kò sí oúnjẹ tí ń mú ara lókun bí èyí tí a jẹ sẹ́nu ẹni lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "There is no food that nourishes one's body like that one puts in one's own mouth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kó wó, kó wó, àràbà ò wó; ojú tìrókò.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“May it crash! May it crash!” The silk-cotton tree does not crash; the ìrókò tree is shamed.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kọ̀ǹkọ̀ṣọ̀ọ́ ní bí a ti ṣe òun tó yìí, òún ṣì ń ku èlùbọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The sieve says despite all that has been done to it it still manages to sift yam-flour.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Kùtù-kùtù kì í jíni lẹ́ẹ̀mejì; kùtù-kùtù ní ń jẹ́ òwúrọ̀; biri ní ń jẹ́ alẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Early dawn does not wake one twice; early dawn is the morning; deep darkness is night.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bá tìjà wá odò; kanna-kánná ò bá ti ẹ̀kọ wá oko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The labẹ́labẹ́  plant did not come to the river looking for a fight; the crow did not come to the farm in search of corn gruel.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bẹ̀rù ìjà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The labẹ́labẹ́ plant is not afraid of a fight.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Lékèélékèé gbàràdá, ó gba tẹlòmíràn mọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The cattle egret borrows wonders to perform, and performs enough for itself and others.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Lójú-lójú là ń wo ẹni tí a óò kéwì fún.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is directly in the eyes that one looks at the subject of the praise poem one is performing.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Máà gbíyè lógún; ti ọwọ́ ẹni ní ń tóni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Place not your hopes in inheritance; the product of one's hand labor is what sustains one.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Má kọjá mi Olùgbàlà” kì í ṣe orin à-kúnlẹ̀-kọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“Pass me not by, dear Redeemer” is not a song one sings on one's knees.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Màrìwò ò wí fúnra wọn tẹ́lẹ̀ tí wọ́n fi ń yọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Palm fronds do not consult with one another before they sprout.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Màrìwò ò wojú ẹnìkan, àfi Ọlọ́run.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Palm fronds look up to no one except God.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Mo di arúgbó ọdẹ tí ńtu olú, mo di àgbàlagbà ọdẹ tí ń wa ògòǹgò láàtàn; mo di ògbólógbòó akítì tí ń gba ìbọn lọ́wọ́ ọdẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "I have become an aged hunter reduced to gathering mushrooms; I have become an old hunter good only for digging palm-weevils; I have become an aged monkey that snatches the gun from the hunter's grip.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Mo kúgbé” lehoro ń dún lóko; “Mo mówó rá” làparò ń dún lábà-a bàbà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“I have perished!” is the cry of the hare in the bush; “I have destroyed things worth a lot of money!” is the cry of the partridge in the guinea-corn field.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Mo ṣe é tán” ló níyì; a kì í dúpẹ́ aláṣekù.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“I have completed the job” is what deserves praise; one does not thank people who leave a job only half done.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Múlele múlèle: ilá tí ò mú lele ò léè so; ikàn tí ò mú lele ò léè wẹ̀wù ẹ̀jẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "High potency upon high potency: the okro that lacks high potency cannot fruit; the bitter tomato that lacks high potency cannot achieve the blood-red complexion.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “N ó lọ, ng ó lọ!” lobìnrín fi ń dẹ́rù ba ọkùnriń “Bóo lè lọ o lọ” lọkùnrín fi ń dẹ́rù ba obìnrin.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“I will leave you, I will leave you!” is the threat a woman flings at a man; “If you have a mind to leave, go ahead and leave!” is the retort a man throws at a woman.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ní inú ẹ̀gún, ní inúu gọ̀gọ̀, ọmọ ayò a ṣara bòró.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "In the midst of thorns, in the midst of crooked twigs, the ayò seeds remain smooth.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ní inú òfíì àti ọ̀láà, ọmọ páńdọ̀rọ̀ ń gbó.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Despite being blown hither and tither in the gale, the fruits of the sausage tree survive to maturity.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ní inú òwú la ti ń bù ṣènì òwú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is out of one's stock of cotton that one takes some for makeweight.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ní ọjọ́ eré nìyà ń dun ọ̀lẹ; kàkà kó wọlé kó jáde a fọwọ́ rọ igi, a pòṣé ṣàrà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is on the day of festivities that the lazy person is miserable; instead of going inside his room and emerging again “in other words, fetching gifts for the revelers” he leans his arms against a tree and hisses incessantly.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ní teere, ní tèèrè, Ṣàngó ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ ó jó wọjà.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Erratically, with almost imperceptible forward movement, just so Ṣàngó danced until he was at the market.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ò báà kúrú, ò báà párí, gbèsè ò sí, ẹ̀sín ò sí; onígbèsè ló lè fini ṣẹ̀sín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "One may be diminutive, and one may be bald, but without debt one has not earned ridicule; only one's creditor has grounds to make fun of one.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó di ọjọ́ tí àkàrà ìyá kùtà ká tó mọ ọmọ tó lè jẹ̀kọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is only on the day when the mother's bean fritters do not sell that one knows which child can consume large quantities of corn-meal.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó gbọ́ tiyán sògìrì mọ́dìí; o gbọ́ toko sọ àdá nù.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "On hearing about pounded yam he girded himself with cooked melon seeds for stew seasoning; on hearing about farm work he threw his cutlass away.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: O kò gun ẹṣin lọ́sàn-án, o ò gun èèyàn lóru, o ò du nǹkan kàrà-kàrà; báwo lo ṣe lè ní káyé má fọ̀ọ́?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You do not ride a horse by day, you do not ride people by night, and you do not make great exertions to achieve any goal; how could you have a say in saving the world from disaster?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: O kò ṣá igi lọ́gbẹ́, o ò sọ ògùrọ̀ lọ́fà, o dédìí ọ̀pẹ o gbẹ́nu sókè ò ń retí; ọ̀fẹ́ ní ńro?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You did not slash the trunk with a cutlass, you did not shoot an arrow at the top of the palm-wine producing palm-tree, you come to the foot of the palm-tree and you raise your open mouth; does it drip all by itself?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: “Ó kù díẹ̀ kí n wí”: ojo ní ń ssọni da.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "“I was just on the verge of speaking my mind”: it only makes one into a coward.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó ní ibi tí ó ń dé, itọ́-dídámì nínú ààwẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It goes some way “in assuaging hunger”, saliva swallowing during a fast.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: O ní kí o gbó ogbó Olúàṣo; o lè jìyà bí Olúàṣo?
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "You pray to live as long as Olúàṣo, but can you endure the trials of Olúàṣo?", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ó pa obì, ó yọ abidún-un rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "He split the kolanut pod open and also removed the bad among the seeds.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Obìnrin tí yó fẹ̀ẹ́ alágbára, ọkàn kan ní ń mú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A woman who would marry a formidable man must have an unwavering mind.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Obìnrin tẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ yẹ ọkọ ẹ̀ níjọ́ ijó, obìnrin gìdìgbà-á yẹ ọkọ ẹ̀ níjọ́ èbù; bó bá ru ọgọ́rùnún èbù tán a kó kébé-kébé níwájú ọkọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A slender woman is the joy of her husband on a day of dancing, but a hefty woman is her husband's joy on the day of yams quartered for planting; after she has totted a hundred yam pieces, she walks smartly “towards the farm” ahead of her husband.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Òbúrẹ́wà ẹni, tòrìṣà ni; àìraṣọlò, tolúwarẹ̀ ni.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A person's ugliness is the god's doing; the person's lack of clothing is his/her own fault.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odídẹrẹ́ kì í kú sóko ìwájẹ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The parrot never dies in the grazing field.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odò kì í kún bo ẹja lójú.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A river does not so swell as to be over the head of the fish.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odò tí a bá mọ orísun ẹ̀ kì í gbéni lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A river whose source one knows does not carry one away.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Odó tó bá tojú ẹni kún kì í gbéni lọ.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A river that swells in one's presence does not carry one away.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Oògùn kì í gbé inú àdó jẹ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "A magical charm does not work from within its gourdlet.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogun kì í jà kó wọlé Asẹ́yín.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "War does not rage and destroy the home of the Asẹ́yìn.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogun kì í rí ẹ̀yìn ogun.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "An army does not see the rear of an(other) army.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ogún ọdún tí ebí ti ń pa ọ̀gà, ìrìn-in fàájì ò padà lẹ́sẹ̀ẹ rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "In all the twenty years that the cameleon has been in the throes of hunger, its dignified gait has not deserted it.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ògbógbó àwọ̀n ní ń bi ajáko.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "It is a mighty net that can trip the civet-cat.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun kan ladìẹ ń jẹ kágbàdo tó dé.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "The chicken had something to eat before there was corn.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a bá gbìn la ó kàá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "What one plants is what one reaps.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a bá gbìn sẹ́yìn la ó padà bá.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever one sows behind one is what one will return to find.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tí a fún ẹ̀ṣọ́ ṣọ́ ni ẹ̀ṣọ́ ń ṣọ́.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever one hands to a warrior to look after is what he looks after.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó ṣe ìjímèrè tó fi gungi ẹ̀gẹ̀: bí kò bá rí ohun tó jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ kò ní sọ̀kalẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever sent the brown monkey climbing to the top of the thorny acacia tree: unless it sees something even more terrifying it will not climb down.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun tó ṣe ìwọ̀fà tí kò fi wá sóko olówó, bójú bá kan ojú yó sọ fún olówóo rẹ̀.
jsonb_data: {"source": "Yoruba Proverbs", "genre": "proverb", "english_translation": "Whatever caused the pawned worker to stay away from the creditor's farm, when the two come face to face he will have some explaining to do.", "origin": "MENYO-20k (Adelani et al. 2021)", "license": "CC BY-NC 4.0", "dialect_assigned_default": true}

headword: Ohun títán lọdún eégún.
